Degree-hours from hourly temperatures

Source: R/degree_days.R
degree_hours.Rd

Computes the thermal contribution of each hourly observation above a base temperature, optionally bounded by an upper threshold with the same cutoff conventions as degree_days().

Usage

degree_hours(
  temperature,
  base = 10,
  upper = NULL,
  cutoff = c("horizontal", "vertical", "intermediate"),
  by_day = FALSE
)

Arguments

temperature

Numeric vector (or matrix, one row per series) of hourly temperatures in degrees Celsius.

base

Lower developmental threshold (degrees Celsius).

upper

Optional upper developmental threshold (degrees Celsius).

cutoff

Upper threshold treatment: "horizontal" (default), "vertical" or "intermediate". Ignored when upper is NULL.

by_day

If TRUE, the hourly series is summed in consecutive blocks of 24 values and divided by 24, returning degree-days per day. The series length must then be a multiple of 24.

Value

Degree-hours (degree Celsius hour) with the shape of temperature, or degree-days per day (degree Celsius day) when by_day = TRUE.

Details

The result is in degree Celsius hour. Divide daily sums by 24 to express them as degree-days: \(GDD_d = \sum_{h=1}^{24} DH_h / 24\). The function assumes regular one-hour time steps; it does not check timestamps.

Examples

temp <- 12 + 8 * sin(2 * pi * (0:23 - 9) / 24)
degree_hours(temp, base = 10)
#>  [1]  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
#>  [8]  0.000000  0.000000  2.000000  4.070552  6.000000  7.656854  8.928203
#> [15]  9.727407 10.000000  9.727407  8.928203  7.656854  6.000000  4.070552
#> [22]  2.000000  0.000000  0.000000
degree_hours(temp, base = 10, by_day = TRUE)
#> [1] 3.615251
